senses.gloss: A decorative strip or band running along the edge of something.
examples: The tablecloth has a red *border* stitched along the edge.
She picked wallpaper with a floral *border* near the ceiling.
Photos printed with white *borders* look old-fashioned now.

senses.gloss: A dull person who tires everyone out with uninteresting talk.
examples: Her uncle is a terrible *bore* at parties.
Don't be such a *bore* — come dance with us.
The panel was two *bores* reading their slides out loud.

senses.gloss: A powerful enemy that must be beaten at the end of a level in a video game.
examples: It took us six tries to beat the final *boss*.
Every level ends with a *boss* that has its own attack pattern.
The later *bosses* are almost impossible without upgrades.

senses.gloss: The part of the body you sit on, in mild everyday speech.
examples: The toddler landed on his *bottom* and laughed.
She wiped the baby's *bottom* and put on a clean diaper.
These jeans are too tight across the *bottom*.

senses.gloss: A strong man employed by a bar or club to keep out or throw out troublemakers.
examples: The *bouncer* checked our IDs at the door.
Two *bouncers* walked the drunk guy outside.
He worked as a *bouncer* while he was in college.

senses.gloss: A large, generous supply of something, especially food from the land or sea.
examples: The table was loaded with the *bounty* of the fall harvest.
Families here still live off the *bounty* of the bay.
Our garden gave us a summer *bounty* of tomatoes and squash.

senses.gloss: The smell of a wine.
examples: This red has a *bouquet* of cherry and black pepper.
He swirled the glass and breathed in the *bouquet*.
Aging in oak gives the wine a richer *bouquet*.

senses.gloss: A boxing or wrestling match.
examples: The title *bout* went all twelve rounds.
He lost his first professional *bout* on points.
Two heavyweight *bouts* are on the card tonight.

senses.gloss: A curved piece of wood with a tight string, used to shoot arrows.
examples: He drew the *bow* and let the arrow fly.
The museum displays *bows* made by Plains hunters.
She practices with a *bow* at the archery range every Saturday.

senses.gloss: The thin stick with stretched hairs that is drawn across the strings of a violin or cello.
examples: She raised her *bow* and the orchestra began.
A good *bow* can cost as much as the violin itself.
He rubbed rosin along the *bow* before the concert.

senses.gloss: A medium-sized dog with a short brown coat and a flat, wrinkled face.
examples: Their *boxer* jumps on everyone who walks in.
*Boxers* need a lot of exercise every day.
We adopted a three-year-old *boxer* from the shelter.

senses.gloss: Loose men's underpants with short legs, always used in the plural.
examples: He answered the door in *boxers* and a T-shirt.
I bought a three-pack of striped *boxers*.
Cotton *boxers* are cooler in the summer.

senses.gloss: A piece of wood or metal fixed across a structure to hold it steady.
examples: The carpenter nailed a diagonal *brace* to the wall frame.
Steel *braces* keep the old church from leaning any further.
Put a *brace* under that shelf so it doesn't sag.

senses.gloss: A very clever person, especially the one who thinks up and directs a plan.
examples: Her older sister was always the *brain* of the family.
He's the *brains* behind the whole app.
The lab hired the best *brains* in the field.

senses.gloss: A mark burned into an animal's hide to show who owns it.
examples: Every calf on the ranch carries the same *brand*.
The *brand* on the horse's flank matched the county records.
Cattle thieves used to alter *brands* with a hot iron.

senses.gloss: A particular kind or style of something that belongs to one person or group.
examples: His *brand* of humor isn't for everyone.
Voters seem tired of that *brand* of politics.
The team plays a rough, physical *brand* of basketball.

senses.gloss: The instruments of a band or orchestra that are made of brass, such as trumpets and trombones.
examples: The *brass* came in too loud in the second movement.
She plays in the *brass* section of the marching band.
The arrangement is heavy on *brass* and drums.

senses.gloss: The highest-ranking officers or officials in an organization.
examples: The *brass* flew in from headquarters to watch the drill.
Department *brass* refused to comment on the case.
Nobody tells the top *brass* what they don't want to hear.

senses.gloss: A gap or hole torn in a wall, dam, or other barrier.
examples: Floodwater poured through a *breach* in the levee.
Soldiers pushed through the *breach* in the city wall.
Crews worked all night to close the *breach*.

senses.gloss: The wide range of subjects or activities that something covers.
examples: The *breadth* of his reading surprised the committee.
The program is praised for its *breadth* rather than its depth.
Few candidates bring that *breadth* of experience.

senses.gloss: A place where something has cracked apart or been interrupted.
examples: The X-ray showed a clean *break* just above his wrist.
We waited for a *break* in the clouds to take off.
The dogs got out through a *break* in the fence.

senses.gloss: A sudden piece of good luck or a chance to succeed.
examples: That role was her big *break*.
Detectives finally caught a *break* in the case.
All he needs is one lucky *break*.

senses.gloss: A switch that cuts off an electrical circuit when it carries too much current.
examples: The space heater tripped the *breaker* again.
Flip the *breaker* before you change that outlet.
The *breakers* are in a gray box in the garage.

senses.gloss: Something that is very easy to do.
examples: The final exam turned out to be a *breeze*.
With the new software, payroll is a *breeze*.
The hike looked hard, but it was a *breeze*.

senses.gloss: The bony ridge at the top of the nose, between the eyes.
examples: His glasses left a red mark on the *bridge* of his nose.
She pinched the *bridge* of her nose and sighed.
The ball broke the *bridge* of his nose in two places.

senses.gloss: A card game for four players in two teams.
examples: My grandparents play *bridge* every Thursday night.
She belongs to a *bridge* club downtown.
He taught me *bridge* the summer I turned twelve.

senses.gloss: The raised platform on a ship from which the captain gives orders.
examples: The captain stayed on the *bridge* all night.
Three officers were on the *bridge* when the storm hit.
Passengers are not allowed on the *bridge*.

senses.gloss: The top edge of a cup, bowl, or other container.
examples: He filled the glass right to the *brim*.
Coffee slopped over the *brim* of the mug.
The bucket was full to the *brim* with rainwater.

senses.gloss: A strong regional accent, especially an Irish or Scottish one.
examples: He answered in a thick Irish *brogue*.
Her *brogue* got stronger when she was tired.
You could hear the *brogue* in the way he said the word.

senses.gloss: A young chicken raised for its meat.
examples: The farm raises about ten thousand *broilers* a year.
*Broiler* prices rose after the feed shortage.
A *broiler* reaches market weight in about six weeks.

senses.gloss: A bronze medal, awarded for third place.
examples: She took *bronze* in the 400 meters.
The team settled for *bronze* after losing the semifinal.
He has two golds and a *bronze* from the last games.

senses.gloss: The forehead.
examples: He wiped the sweat from his *brow*.
Her *brow* wrinkled as she read the letter.
A cold cloth on the *brow* brought the fever down.

senses.gloss: Rough low bushes and small trees growing thickly on open land.
examples: The rabbit disappeared into the *brush*.
Crews cleared the *brush* along the highway to slow the fire.
We piled the cut *brush* behind the barn.

senses.gloss: A short, close encounter with something dangerous or unpleasant.
examples: He had a *brush* with the law as a teenager.
Her *brush* with cancer changed the way she works.
The pilot describes his *brush* with death in the first chapter.

senses.gloss: A period when prices rise far above what things are really worth, before falling sharply.
examples: The housing *bubble* burst in 2008.
Analysts keep warning about a *bubble* in tech stocks.
Every *bubble* looks obvious once it has popped.

senses.gloss: A closed-off world that keeps out the wider reality.
examples: Students live in a *bubble* on campus.
Officials inside the Washington *bubble* lose touch with voters.
The team spent the season in a *bubble*, tested daily and cut off from fans.

senses.gloss: A friendly word for a man or boy, used when speaking to him.
examples: Hey, *bud*, you dropped your wallet.
Thanks, *bud* — I owe you one.
Watch where you're going, *bud*.

senses.gloss: A part of a computer's memory that holds data briefly while it is being moved or played.
examples: The video froze while the *buffer* filled.
Sound is copied into a *buffer* before it reaches the speakers.
A full *buffer* can crash the whole program.

senses.gloss: A mistake in a computer program that makes it behave wrongly.
examples: The update fixed a *bug* that erased saved files.
Testers filed a dozen *bugs* on the first day.
There's a *bug* in the checkout page.

senses.gloss: A minor infection passed from one person to another.
examples: Half the office caught a stomach *bug*.
She's home with some kind of *bug*.
A nasty *bug* went through the daycare in January.

senses.gloss: A tiny hidden microphone used to listen in secretly.
examples: Agents planted a *bug* in the hotel room.
They swept the office for *bugs* every month.
A *bug* under the table recorded the whole meeting.

senses.gloss: A gradual increase in the number or strength of something.
examples: The country announced a military *buildup* along its border.
A slow *buildup* of pressure finally cracked the pipe.
Doctors watched for a *buildup* of fluid in his lungs.

senses.gloss: The stretch of preparation and excitement before a big event.
examples: The *buildup* to the Super Bowl lasts two weeks.
There was so much *buildup* that the movie couldn't live up to it.
In the *buildup* to the election, both sides spent heavily.

senses.gloss: The greater part of something.
examples: The *bulk* of the money went to salaries.
She spent the *bulk* of her career overseas.
The *bulk* of the crowd had already gone home.

senses.gloss: Nonsense, or something said that is plainly untrue. Informal.
examples: That excuse is a bunch of *bull*.
He fed us a lot of *bull* about being sick.
Cut the *bull* and tell me what really happened.

senses.gloss: An investor who expects prices to rise.
examples: *Bulls* argue that the rally still has room to run.
He has been a *bull* on energy stocks all year.
The *bulls* pushed the index to a record close.

senses.gloss: A dot marking one item in a list, or the short line of text beside it.
examples: Put your main results in three *bullets*.
No slide should have more than five *bullets*.
She rewrote the paragraph as a set of *bullets*.

senses.gloss: A small increase in an amount or level.
examples: Everyone got a small *bump* in pay this year.
The ad campaign gave sales a nice *bump*.
Polls showed a *bump* for the governor after the speech.

senses.gloss: Hair gathered and twisted into a round knot at the back of the head.
examples: She twisted her hair into a *bun* before her shift.
Dancers wear their hair in tight *buns*.
He pulled his long hair up into a messy *bun*.

senses.gloss: A hollow filled with sand on a golf course, placed to catch bad shots.
senses.ru: бункер (песчаная ловушка на поле для гольфа)
examples: His tee shot rolled into the *bunker*.
She got up and down from the greenside *bunker*.
The new course has sixty *bunkers*.

senses.gloss: A sharp, clever insult. Informal.
examples: Ouch — that was a *burn*.
Her reply was the *burn* of the night.
He laughed off the *burn* and kept talking.

senses.gloss: A cheap phone or account used for a short time and then thrown away.
examples: He called her from a *burner*.
The dealer switched to a new *burner* every month.
She set up a *burner* just to sign up for free trials.

senses.gloss: The short end left when a cigarette has been smoked.
examples: He crushed the *butt* under his heel.
*Butts* littered the sidewalk outside the bar.
There were three *butts* in the ashtray.

senses.gloss: The person or thing that a joke is aimed at.
examples: He was the *butt* of every joke in the locker room.
Her accent made her the *butt* of jokes at school.
Nobody enjoys being the *butt* of the family's teasing.

senses.gloss: A pleasant feeling of excitement or of being slightly drunk.
examples: Two beers gave him a nice *buzz*.
There's a real *buzz* when you walk out on stage.
The coffee gave me a *buzz* that lasted all morning.

senses.gloss: An operation that routes blood around a blocked artery of the heart.
examples: He had a triple *bypass* last spring.
*Bypass* surgery kept her in the hospital for a week.
The doctor recommended a *bypass* rather than a stent.

senses.gloss: The part of a truck, train, or crane where the driver sits.
examples: He climbed up into the *cab* of the semi.
The *cab* of the tractor has air conditioning.
Two men were riding in the *cab* of the locomotive.

senses.gloss: The part of a plane or ship where the passengers sit or sleep.
examples: The crew walked through the *cabin* before takeoff.
Our *cabin* on the ship had one small window.
*Cabin* pressure dropped and the masks came down.

senses.gloss: Television delivered to homes through wires, and the service that supplies it.
examples: We canceled *cable* and stream everything now.
The game is only on *cable*.
Our *cable* bill went up again this year.

senses.gloss: Someone who carries a golfer's clubs and advises on shots during a round.
examples: His *caddy* handed him a seven iron.
She worked as a *caddy* at the country club in high school.
The *caddies* walked ahead to read the green.

senses.gloss: A flat, pressed block of something such as soap, or of food shaped and fried.
examples: A *cake* of soap sat on the edge of the tub.
We ordered crab *cakes* to start.
She fried the leftover rice into small *cakes*.

senses.gloss: The level of quality or ability of a person or thing.
examples: A player of his *caliber* doesn't come along often.
The school attracts teachers of very high *caliber*.
We need someone of the same *caliber* to replace her.

senses.gloss: A cat with a coat of white, black, and orange patches.
examples: Our *calico* sleeps on the windowsill all day.
Almost all *calicos* are female.
The shelter had two kittens and an older *calico*.

senses.gloss: The cry of a bird or animal.
examples: The *call* of a loon carried across the lake.
He can imitate a dozen bird *calls*.
We heard the *call* of geese somewhere overhead.

senses.gloss: A decision or judgment, especially a referee's ruling.
examples: The ref made a bad *call* in the final minute.
Whether we go is your *call*.
It was a tough *call*, but we canceled the trip.
